blocks.x: Where most programs improvise, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration as we deliver it is sequenced: Hundreds of agents as one governed fleet — roles, queues, budgets and audit for the AI workforce. The sequence matters more than the stack — both are documented here.
What we deliver under this name

Scaling from five agents to five hundred breaks ad-hoc patterns: conflicts over shared systems, duplicated work, no cost accountability, no way to know which agent did what. We build the orchestration layer that treats agents as a managed workforce — role definitions, task queues and bidding, shared-memory contracts, per-team budgets, kill switches, and a control tower showing fleet health, throughput and cost per completed task.

The orchestration core runs on durable execution (Temporal-class runtimes) with idempotent task semantics, priority lanes for SLA-bound work, and a policy engine that routes high-risk actions to approval workflows. Fleet upgrades are staged like software releases: shadow mode, canary cohorts, and automatic rollback on eval regression.

Programs of Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration run in Technology & SaaS, Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Logistics & Supply Chain — always against one named number, always with the baseline signed first.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Fleet control tower
health, throughput, cost and policy-violation telemetry across all agents
Role & queue architecture
agent roles, task bidding, priority lanes and SLA routing
Shared-memory contracts
blackboard and state-store patterns preventing work duplication
Budget & metering
per-team, per-role token and action budgets with chargeback
Staged rollout machinery
shadow, canary and cohort releases with automatic rollback
